title: Don't Pass@k: A Bayesian Framework for Large Language Model Evaluation
one_liner: 把多次模型评测结果建模为分类计数，用 Dirichlet 后验报告加权表现与不确定性，并比较有限采样下的模型排名稳定性。

problem.text: 有限运行预算下，如何比较模型表现，并说明榜单分数差距是否足以区分模型？本文研究 LLM 评测指标和不确定性报告，本身不是一个新的 Agent 任务环境。实验使用模拟数据和数学推理测试集。

gap.text: Pass@k 估计 k 次尝试至少一次成功，作者指出其在样本少、k 接近总尝试次数时可能导致不稳定排名。单独报告平均正确率也无法表达估计精度，且难以统一处理格式、部分得分等分类结果。本文将表现估计和不确定性一起报告。

method.text: 先保存 M 道题、每题 N 次运行的结果矩阵，将结果分成 C+1 类并指定权重；按题将分类计数更新到 Dirichlet 后验，计算整体加权表现的后验均值 μ 和标准差 σ。均匀先验、二元评分且每题同样 N 次时，单题均值为 (正确次数+1)/(N+2)；作者证明该设置下点估计排序与平均准确率一致。后验矩的解析计算，与后续区间或排名近似须区分。

trace.text: 论文的偏置硬币模拟先设定 11 个模型替身的真实答对概率，并对 30 道题重复采样。示例中两个替身的平均真实成功率约为 0.608 和 0.6213；80 次运行能给出点估计先后，但纳入不确定性后仍可能无法可靠区分。已知真值的模拟用来检查估计排名，真实模型实验则只能使用有限采样参考排名。

inputs_outputs.text: 输入是按题组织的分类评分矩阵、类别权重，以及可选的历史结果先验；输出是加权表现估计、标准差和带不确定性的模型比较。附录还展示格式合规、正确性及效率等评分方案。方法需要已有可用的判分信号，不能直接从任意文本自动决定科学答案是否正确。

results.text: v1 使用 11 个模型配置，在 AIME 2024/2025、HMMT 2025 和 BrUMO 2025 上每配置每题运行 80 次，并与 Pass@2/4/8 等方法比较。图 1 报告 HMMT 和 BrUMO 的平均收敛尝试次数：Pass 方法约 69.5、48.5，Bayes@N 约 44.2、27.1；这里的收敛是相对有限样本参考排名定义的。均匀先验下 Bayes@N 与平均准确率排序相同，不能把收益描述为它总能产生不同且更好的点估计排序。

contributions.text: 将二元与多类别、加权 rubric 的结果纳入同一后验推断框架，给出表现均值和方差的解析表达。作者还讨论以不确定性辅助模型排名、使用历史证据作为先验，以及用模拟与实际测试集检查排名随预算变化的稳定性。贡献属于评价方法和工具，而非一组新的 Agent 任务。

limitations.text: 作者明确说明，该方法处理有限样本造成的统计不确定性，不修复数据集偏差、分布变化或评分规则错误。真实模型的参考排名来自最多 80 次试验，不是已知的无限采样真值。§2.5 对整体后验形状及 z 分数比较使用大题量下的高斯近似，因此解析均值方差并不意味着任意小样本的区间和名次都有无条件精确保证。

cost.text: 后验均值和方差可从计数解析更新，但产生评测样本仍然需要推理资源。附录 F 报告温度 0.6、top-p 0.95、每数据集/模型 80 次试验、最多 32,768 输出 token，并使用 8 张 NVIDIA H200 的计算集群；没有给出统一的每模型美元成本。

relevance.text: 知识库分析：作为 benchmark 评分与报告方法的背景文献收录。它有助于读懂论文中的重复次数、聚合指标和排名不确定性，但实验主体是数学推理模型，不应直接宣称已在完整 Agent 工作流上验证。

en.one_liner: A Dirichlet posterior turns repeated evaluation outcomes into weighted performance estimates and uncertainty, allowing model rankings to be compared under limited sampling.

sections.problem: With a limited evaluation budget, how can we compare models and tell whether a score gap distinguishes them? This paper studies LLM evaluation metrics and uncertainty reporting. Its experiments use simulations and mathematical-reasoning test sets.
sections.gap: Pass@k estimates the chance of at least one success in k attempts. The authors argue that rankings can be unstable with few samples, especially as k approaches the total number of attempts. Mean accuracy alone does not express precision and does not readily cover categorical outcomes such as formatting and partial credit.
sections.method: The method stores an M-question by N-run outcome matrix, assigns outcomes to C+1 classes and specifies class weights. Per-question counts update Dirichlet posteriors, from which it computes the posterior mean μ and standard deviation σ of aggregate weighted performance. With a uniform prior, binary scores and equal N, a question’s mean is (correct count+1)/(N+2). In that setting the point-estimate ordering matches mean accuracy. Analytic moments must be distinguished from approximations for intervals and rankings.
sections.trace: A biased-coin simulation gives 11 model stand-ins known success probabilities and samples repeated answers to 30 questions. Two example stand-ins have mean true success rates of about 0.608 and 0.6213. After 80 runs, point estimates can order them even when uncertainty prevents a reliable distinction. Simulations have known truth, whereas real-model experiments use a finite-sample reference ranking.
sections.inputs_outputs: Inputs are per-question categorical score matrices, category weights and optionally a prior based on previous results. Outputs include weighted performance estimates, standard deviations and uncertainty-aware comparisons. The appendix covers formatting, correctness and efficiency rubrics. A usable scoring signal must already exist. The method does not decide the scientific validity of arbitrary text.
sections.results: Version 1 evaluates 11 model configurations on AIME 2024/2025, HMMT 2025 and BrUMO 2025 with 80 runs per configuration per question, comparing with Pass@2/4/8 and other methods. Figure 1 gives average attempts to converge on HMMT and BrUMO of about 69.5 and 48.5 for Pass methods versus 44.2 and 27.1 for Bayes@N. Convergence is defined against a finite-sample reference ranking. Under a uniform prior, Bayes@N and mean accuracy have the same point-estimate ordering.
sections.contributions: The paper puts binary, multiclass and weighted-rubric scores into one posterior framework, deriving analytic expressions for the performance mean and variance. It explores uncertainty-aware ranking and historical priors, and tests ranking stability as budgets change in simulations and real test sets.
sections.limitations: The method addresses finite-sample uncertainty. It does not correct dataset bias, distribution shifts or faulty scoring rules. Real-model reference rankings use at most 80 trials rather than known infinite-sample truth. Section 2.5 uses a large-question-count Gaussian approximation for posterior shape and z-score comparisons, so exact moments do not imply unconditional small-sample guarantees for intervals or ranks.
sections.cost: Posterior moments update analytically from counts, but collecting outcomes still costs inference. Appendix F reports temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, 80 trials per dataset/model and up to 32,768 output tokens, using a cluster with eight NVIDIA H200 GPUs. No uniform per-model dollar cost is given.
sections.relevance: Library analysis. This is background on benchmark scoring and reporting. It helps interpret repetitions, aggregate metrics and ranking uncertainty. The experiments concern mathematical-reasoning models and do not establish validation on complete agent workflows.

related.scienceagentbench: ScienceAgentBench reports repeated runs and aggregation. This method examines how sampling and metrics affect model comparisons, using different experimental tasks and measurement targets.
